user.title: OCPP Hub
user.description: Set the port your charger connects to. In the charger's OCPP profile, use ws:// followed by the address of this Home Assistant, a colon and this port.

data_description.port: The TCP port the OCPP server listens on. A port above 1024 needs no special rights.

abort.single_instance_allowed: OCPP Hub is already set up.

init.title: Vendor backend mirror
init.description: Pass a read-only copy of everything the charger says to the manufacturer's own backend, so its app keeps working. The manufacturer can look but never control the charger. Leave the address empty to switch the mirror off.

data_description.vendor_url: Starts with ws:// or wss:// and holds the host, the port and the path of the manufacturer's OCPP backend, without the charger's serial number and without credentials.
data_description.vendor_user: Only if the backend asks for a user name. Set a password with it.
data_description.vendor_password: Never shown again. Leave empty to keep the stored password; it is only kept while the host of the address stays the same.
data_description.max_current: The highest current per phase the hub may ask the charger for. Keep it below the installer's own limit. A value under 6 A in the charge limit pauses the charger.
data_description.vendor_commands: What happens to commands from the manufacturer's backend. Passing them on lets it start and stop charges, change a few settings, set charging profiles, unlock the cable, set the connector inoperative and use its own DataTransfer channel, within the current ceiling below. Reset, firmware and diagnostics stay refused.
data_description.schedule_entity: A schedule helper of Home Assistant. Its blocks are the times in which the charger may charge. Pressing the apply-schedule button writes it to the charger; changing the helper writes nothing.
data_description.schedule_inside_a: The current while a block is on. Leave empty to use your ceiling; a block can carry its own limit as data (limit).
data_description.schedule_outside_a: The current when no block is on. Leave empty to pause the charger (0 A). Under 6 A pauses.

error.invalid_url: The address must start with ws:// or wss:// and name a host.
error.credentials_in_url: Remove the user name and password from the address and use the fields below.
error.credentials_incomplete: Set both a user name and a password, or neither.

no_hub_loaded.message: OCPP Hub is not loaded, so there is no charge history to read yet.

control_not_connected.message: The charger is not connected, so nothing can be sent to it.

control_above_ceiling.message: Refused: {detail}. Raise the ceiling in the integration options if the installation allows it.

control_no_charge.message: No charge is running, so there is nothing to stop.

charger_not_chosen.message: More than one charger (or none) is known; name the charger with charger_id.

schedule_helper_unavailable.message: The schedule helper is missing or unavailable.

get_sessions.name: Get charge sessions
get_sessions.description: Returns the stored charge sessions, newest first. The history is never truncated.

charger_id.name: Charger ID
charger_id.description: Only the sessions of this charger. Leave empty for all.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Return at most this many of the newest sessions.

set_schedule.name: Set charge schedule
set_schedule.description: Installs a daily schedule of charge limits on the charger, repeated every day from midnight local time. It replaces the single charge limit. Every limit stays under your current ceiling, and a limit under 6 A pauses the charger. Changes of summer and winter time shift it by an hour until you set it again.

charger_id.name: Charger ID
charger_id.description: The charger to write to. Leave empty when there is only one.

periods.name: Periods
periods.description: A list of periods, each with a time of the day (HH:MM) and the limit in amperes that applies from then on. The first period starts at 00:00 and the times must increase.

options.forward: Pass them on to the charger
